purpose: Traceable reproduction fixture for the paper's selected optimum, with every input carrying its provenance and every criterion carrying its justification.

model.parameter_set_provenance: Table 2 as printed, p. 4, loaded as a fitted set; nothing here is refit

solver.h_max_reason: chosen from the reported kLa = 133 h^-1 so h*kLa = 1.33 stays inside the explicit RK4 stability limit

experiment.selected: the optimised fed-batch process the paper selected from its Pareto front
why_this_one: It is the only configuration in the paper that appears with experimental data (Fig. 5), so it can be compared against both the authors' model prediction and their measurements.
Its feed recipe is reported in full (17.5 % w/v glycerol, 24.5 % w/v yeast extract, 0.72 mL/h), so no feed quantity has to be inferred.
Fig. 3, the held-out validation experiment, has a different feed recipe; it is used here as a secondary comparison, not as the primary target.
Fig. 2 is the fitting experiment. Its parameters were tuned against it, so it is NOT independent evidence and is recorded as such rather than compared against.

reported_endpoints.biomass_24h_source: Abstract, p. 1: 'The optimized process yielded 20.7 g dry cell weight/L'
reported_endpoints.biomass_range_source: 3.3, p. 7: 'The biomass concentrations achieved in 24 h were 19.9-21.5 g DCW/L'
reported_endpoints.model_predicted_source: 3.3, p. 7: 'in agreement with the model predicted value of 19.44 g DCW/L'

X0.source: printed p. 2, 2.2: initial culture optical density (OD600) of 0.05
X0.note: The paper prints no OD600-to-dry-cell-weight calibration, so this g/L value cannot be derived from the reported OD600. 0.05 g/L is a typical E. coli figure and is declared here as an assumption, not as a paper value. It is one of the sensitivity cases below.

S2_0.source: printed p. 2, 2.2: SOB medium contains tryptone 20 g/L and yeast extract 5 g/L
S2_0.note: The paper states the medium recipe but never states the model's initial complex-substrate concentration. S2 is the model's 'complex nitrogen-rich substrate'; both tryptone and yeast extract are complex nitrogen-rich substrates, so the whole complex fraction of the stated medium is 20 + 5 = 25 g/L. This is a derivation from a stated recipe, not a reported model input, and the narrower reading (yeast extract alone, 5 g/L) is carried as a sensitivity case.

DO0.source: not stated in the main paper; the paper's own Fig. 5a model curve starts at about 94-95 %
DO0.note: A shake flask filled with medium and left standing is saturated with air, so 100 % is the natural reading and is declared as an assumption. It turns out not to matter: the oxygen balance reaches the same level within about an hour for any starting value between 50 % and 100 %, because the culture's own oxygen demand, not the starting value, sets the dissolved-oxygen level. The `do0_80` case confirms this and the two runs agree to four decimal places.

S1_0.source: printed p. 2, 2.2: 'The initial production medium was supplemented with 2.76 g/L glycerol'
S1_0.note: Reported directly, and the only initial concentration the paper states. The digitized t=0 glycerol marks in Figures 3c and 5d read 2.78 g/L, which cross-checks both the digitization and this value.

V0.source: printed p. 2, 2.3: 'These flasks were filled with 100 mL medium'
V0.note: Reported directly. The same 1:5 fill ratio in the 500 mL baffled flask is what makes kLa = 133 h^-1 the applicable value.

feed.source: printed p. 7, 3.3: 'a feed composition of 17.5% glycerol, 24.5% yeast extract, and a feed rate of 0.72 mL/h'; feeding start from p. 3, 3.1
feed.note: 1 % w/v = 10 g/L is the paper's own convention; 1 mL/h = 1e-3 L/h. Both conversions are stated, not inferred. The feed is supplemented with 2 mM MgCl2/MgSO4 and 2x antibiotic (p. 2); neither enters the model.

operating_conditions_not_modelled.source: printed p. 2, 2.3; Fig. 5b plots pH but draws no model curve

cases.why: the paper-grounded reading of the medium
the narrower reading of S2: yeast extract alone. Included because it is the value the composition example used and because it is the alternative the paper does not resolve.
an upper bound on the complex substrate, to show the endpoint is not saturated in S2
a larger inoculum, to show the initial biomass is not what sets the endpoint
a much larger inoculum, same purpose
a lower starting dissolved oxygen, closer to the start of the paper's own model curve

biomass.role: the authors' plotted model prediction for this configuration

reference.digitization: tools/digitize_figures.py; calibration and uncertainty are stored per panel in the dataset
reference.note: Digitized values are never presented as measurements. They are readings off a raster figure, with their uncertainty, and the comparison uses them as such.

criteria.statement: The culture becomes oxygen-limited after feeding starts: min DO over 6 <= t <= 24 h is below 10 %.
criteria.justification: The paper states it, not the implementation: printed p. 9, 'Based on the results of the DO profile, it is seen that the growth is limited by oxygen availability beyond 6 h.' The paper's own Fig. 3a and Fig. 5a model curves fall to about 1-6 %. Ten per cent is a generous bound that still separates oxygen limitation from substrate limitation: the S2-limited reading reaches a minimum DO of about 60 %, so the criterion discriminates between the two regimes rather than between two close values.

criteria.statement: Final biomass lies inside the paper's own reported experimental range for the 24 h fed-batch trials.
criteria.justification: This is the paper's reported measurement, quoted on p. 7 as the range across the tested proteins and in the abstract as 20.7 g/L. Using the reported range rather than a point value respects the run-to-run spread the paper itself reports, and avoids testing against a single number the paper never isolates. The threshold is a paper quantity; nothing in it was chosen to fit any output.

criteria.statement: The biomass trajectory agrees with the authors' own plotted model prediction over the readable span.
criteria.justification: Two independent figures set the bar. The paper's own model sits about 1 g/L RMS from its own held-out validation data on a trajectory reaching 20 g/L (about 5 %, from the nine digitized Fig. 3b points), so a transcription that computes the same model must land well inside that. The digitization uncertainty on the reference curve is about 0.5 g/L, so 25 % is thirty times the reading noise. A threshold that loose can only fail on a genuine difference between the implemented equations and the printed ones, not on raster noise or solver tolerance.
criteria.comparison_interval: 0.25 h grid over the span where the paper's curve is readable, t = 0..24 h

criteria.statement: Two runs of the same configuration agree.
criteria.justification: The solver is deterministic given identical inputs and parameters. Any divergence above floating-point round-off indicates hidden state or a race, which would invalidate every other comparison. This is a property of the implementation, not of the paper.

status.note: Fixed by this fixture's criteria and the report's conclusion, not by any test outcome. See reports/GANJAVE_SCIENTIFIC_VALIDATION.md.
